learningObjectives: Use Agile Workbench to manage user stories, bugs, and feedback items across features and releases.
Describe CI/CD pipelines, Deployment Manager, and agile development best practices in Pega Platform.

elements.description: Application profile tracks development work; Developer Assistant organizes work and provides AI-assisted aids. The source names Guidance, Knowledge, Work and Checklists tabs without saying every tab is independently AI-powered.
items: Application profile: up-to-date view of all work items, features, and status
Developer Assistant pane: AI-powered aids with 4 tabs — Guidance, Knowledge, Work, Checklists

elements.description: Features = capabilities the application supports. Subfeatures = features nested within a feature. When you create a new Case Type, Pega automatically creates a feature with the same name. Work items are associated with features or subfeatures.
Work items tracked in the Application profile:
items: Stories (User stories): describe business requirements; make up the majority of development work; can be uploaded from Excel in bulk
Bugs: document feature defects; major bugs are addressed before minor ones
Feedback items: enhancement requests identified during playback sessions

elements.term: Two ways to change work item status
elements.description: To do, Doing and Done are the listed statuses. Change status by dragging the card to a column or using the Status list on the work item itself.

Integrates with Agile Studio (expanded functionality: release management, progress tracking, team capacity, analytics). Also integrates with external tools: Jira, CA Agile Central — allowing customers to use their existing infrastructure.

elements.text: CI/CD is like a car assembly line with quality checkpoints. CI is the early part: workers (developers) frequently add parts (code changes), robots (automated tests) check each part before it moves forward. If a part fails inspection, the line STOPS. CD is the downstream line: the car is tested at speed, compatibility, and safety gates before reaching the customer (production). Deployment Manager is the factory floor supervisor who orchestrates the whole line automatically.

elements.description: A collaborative practice between development, quality, and operations:
items: Goal: deliver high-quality software in an automated, agile way
Reduces time to market without compromising quality
CI/CD pipeline = the automated process from development through testing to deployment

elements.description: Developers frequently check in changes. Automated build verifies each change — identifies issues EARLY. 'Ready to share' step: new changes work with existing app. 'Integrate changes' step: critical tests pass → changes published to development repository.
The deployment pipeline stages after CI:
items: Rigorous automated regression testing
Changes deployed to staging for further testing
'Ready to accept': acceptance criteria tests pass
'Ready to deploy': performance and compatibility tests pass
Deploy: validates in preproduction → production → post-deployment tests with rollback option

elements.description: Deployment Manager orchestrates Pega CI/CD. The source describes Admin Studio for designing and managing pipelines and a configured App Studio integration for Publishing.
items: Manage pipelines through Admin Studio in the described workflow.
After integration, App Studio Settings > Versions exposes the application pipeline for Publishing.
Automate Branch merging, packaging and environment promotion.
The source lists Jenkins and Microsoft Azure DevOps as third-party examples.

elements.caption: Release stages and the distinction between pipeline management and App Studio Publishing.

elements.description: ① Real-time updates: frequent small-scope development iterations. ② Testing: continuous validation to identify and address issues early. ③ Branches: concurrent team development environment to maximize productivity.
Best practices for Continuous Integration in Pega:
items: Test early and often: run Pega unit tests + critical integration tests before packaging
If tests fail → STOP the release pipeline until fixed
Automate: trigger merges and builds via Deployment Manager
Update the referenced product Rule (Rule-Admin-Product).
Maintain deployable version history by publishing exported application archives to a repository.

elements.description: ① Create test environments (Docker/UAT). ② Run regression tests — UI and service layer. ③ Use version control: target specific Ruleset versions for production. ④ Define a rollback strategy. ⑤ Annotate passing packages as deployment-ready.

elements.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 760 190" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" font-family="inherit"><title>Delivery quality practices</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="744" height="174" rx="12" fill="var(--pa-surface-2)" stroke="var(--pa-brand)"/><text x="28" y="40" fill="var(--pa-brand)" font-size="16" font-weight="700">Delivery quality practices</text><text x="28" y="78" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)" font-size="14">CI failure: stop progression until fixed; keep the product Rule and archive history current.</text><text x="28" y="110" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)" font-size="14">CD: regression testing, target Ruleset versions, rollback strategy and package annotation.</text><text x="28" y="142" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)" font-size="14">Use Docker or a similar test environment tool; deployment may be manual or automatic.</text></svg>
elements.caption: Source best practices distinguish quality gates, versioned packages and deployment choices; exploratory testing is not assumed fully automated.

examPitfalls.title: Pipeline management and App Studio Publishing are different entry points
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not turn Admin Studio pipeline management into a claim that App Studio cannot interact with Deployment Manager.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Manage pipelines in Admin Studio; properly integrated App Studio exposes Publishing through Settings > Versions.

examPitfalls.title: New Case Type auto-creates a feature with the same name
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks what a developer must do after creating a new Case Type to track it in Agile Workbench. Candidates describe manually creating a Feature — not knowing Pega auto-creates one with the same name.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When you create a new Case Type, Pega automatically creates a feature with the same name in Agile Workbench.

examPitfalls.title: 3 work item types — Feedback ≠ Bug
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The source lists Stories, Bugs and Feedback. Do not discard Feedback or confuse it with a defect; it records playback enhancement requests.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Stories = business requirements. Bugs = feature defects. Feedback items = enhancement requests from playback sessions. These are three distinct types.

examPitfalls.title: CI test failure STOPS the pipeline — do not continue
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A scenario describes a CI pipeline where one test fails. Candidates say 'CI marks it failed but packages and delivers anyway.' CI hard-stops on failure — nothing is packaged or delivered until tests pass.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If tests fail during CI, STOP the release pipeline until the issue is fixed. Do not allow failing changes to proceed.

examPitfalls.title: Status supports dragging and the work item Status list
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Saying drag-only excludes a second documented method.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use either a card drag or the work item Status list for To do, Doing or Done.

examPitfalls.title: CD rollback strategy: if test fails → roll back latest import
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A CD best-practices question asks the correct response to a failed deployment test. Candidates describe retrying or debugging in production. The documented strategy is immediate rollback of the latest import.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If a test fails during CD → roll back the latest import. If all tests pass → annotate the package as ready to deploy.

examPitfalls.title: Agile Studio EXPANDS Agile Workbench — they are not the same tool
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Agile Studio is a separate integrated tool that adds broader project-management capabilities; the source does not describe Workbench as a component inside Agile Studio.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Agile Studio is a SEPARATE tool that expands Agile Workbench with: release management, progress tracking, team capacity, and analytics.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Developer Assistant pane in Agile Workbench has four tabs. Which set correctly identifies all four?

options.text: Guidance, Knowledge, Work, Checklists
Stories, Bugs, Feedback, Checklists
Features, Subfeatures, Work Items, Releases
Guidance, Tasks, Bugs, Releases

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the four named Developer Assistant tabs; distinguish them from work item types.
practiceQuiz.rationale: These are the four named Developer Assistant tabs.

optionExplanations.A: These are the four named Developer Assistant tabs.
optionExplanations.B: Stories, Bugs and Feedback are work item types, not this tab set.
optionExplanations.C: Features and subfeatures organize work, not these four tabs.
optionExplanations.D: Tasks, Bugs and Releases are not the stated tab set.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What happens automatically in Agile Workbench when a developer creates a new Case Type?

options.text: A feature with the same name as the Case Type is automatically created
A user story describing the Case Type is automatically generated
A subfeature is created under the first existing feature
A bug tracking entry is created for the Case Type

practiceQuiz.hint: A new Case Type creates a same-named feature; the source does not promise an epic.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source states a same-named feature is created.

optionExplanations.A: The source states a same-named feature is created.
optionExplanations.B: It does not promise an automatically generated user story.
optionExplanations.C: It specifies a feature, not a subfeature under an existing one.
optionExplanations.D: Creating a Case Type does not automatically log a defect.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During a playback session, a business stakeholder identifies an enhancement they want in a future release. Which work item type should the developer create?

options.text: Feedback item
Bug
User story
Subfeature

practiceQuiz.hint: Enhancement requests from playback sessions have a specific work item type.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Feedback records the playback enhancement request.

optionExplanations.A: Feedback records the playback enhancement request.
optionExplanations.B: A bug records a defect rather than this requested enhancement.
optionExplanations.C: Stories express requirements, but Feedback is the playback type requested.
optionExplanations.D: A subfeature organizes capabilities rather than serving as this work item.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO documented methods change an Agile Workbench work item from To do to Doing?

options.text: Drag the card to the Doing column
Use the Status list on the work item itself
Right-click the card and select Change Status
Use the Developer Assistant pane to update status

practiceQuiz.hint: Agile Workbench organizes user stories and bugs on a Kanban-style board view.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dragging the card to Doing is one documented method. The work item’s Status list is the other documented method.

optionExplanations.A: Dragging the card to Doing is one documented method.
optionExplanations.B: The work item’s Status list is the other documented method.
optionExplanations.C: This context-menu method is not given in the topic.
optionExplanations.D: Developer Assistant is not the documented status-change method.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the source’s workflow, which studio provides Deployment Manager pipeline design and management? This is distinct from Publishing through a configured App Studio integration.

options.text: Admin Studio
App Studio
Dev Studio
Agile Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: It's in the studio focused on platform administration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Admin Studio is the described pipeline-management entry point.

optionExplanations.A: Admin Studio is the described pipeline-management entry point.
optionExplanations.B: Integrated App Studio exposes Publishing, a different task from this question.
optionExplanations.C: Dev Studio is not the entry point identified in this source.
optionExplanations.D: Agile Studio tracks delivery work rather than this pipeline-management interface.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A business stakeholder asks a Pega SA to explain what DevOps means in the context of Pega Platform and how it improves the speed and quality of application delivery compared to traditional siloed development. What is DevOps in the context of Pega Platform?

options.text: A collaborative effort between development, quality, and operations to deliver high-quality software in an automated, agile way
A tool for automating branch merging and application packaging
A methodology that replaces Agile Workbench for release management
A framework that eliminates the need for testing in CI/CD pipelines

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall Pega's definition of DevOps — which three organizational functions does it unite?
practiceQuiz.rationale: DevOps joins development, quality and operations in delivery practice.

optionExplanations.A: DevOps joins development, quality and operations in delivery practice.
optionExplanations.B: A specific automation tool does not define the whole practice.
optionExplanations.C: DevOps is broader than replacing a work-tracking tool.
optionExplanations.D: Quality and testing remain part of the practice.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During continuous integration, unit tests fail for newly introduced changes. According to best practices, what should happen?

options.text: Stop the release pipeline until the issue is fixed
Proceed to packaging and fix in the next sprint
Mark the test as a known issue and continue
Move the changes to staging for further testing

practiceQuiz.hint: Failing tests in CI should block further progress.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Stop the pipeline until the failing test issue is fixed.

optionExplanations.A: Stop the pipeline until the failing test issue is fixed.
optionExplanations.B: Continuing to packaging disregards the stated quality gate.
optionExplanations.C: Labeling a failure does not satisfy this best practice.
optionExplanations.D: Moving failing changes to staging bypasses this CI gate.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which step in the continuous delivery pipeline verifies performance, scale, and compatibility tests before production deployment?

options.text: Ready to deploy
Ready to share
Integrate changes
Ready to accept

practiceQuiz.hint: This step comes just before the actual production deploy.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ready to deploy checks performance, scale and compatibility.

optionExplanations.A: Ready to deploy checks performance, scale and compatibility.
optionExplanations.B: Ready to share checks new changes with the existing application.
optionExplanations.C: Integrate changes ensures critical tests before publication.
optionExplanations.D: Ready to accept checks acceptance criteria instead.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does Deployment Manager help eliminate manual work in a DevOps workflow?

options.text: It automates Branch merging, application packaging, and promoting the application to different environments
It automatically writes user stories based on application configuration
It replaces the need for third-party DevOps tools entirely
It runs production-level testing on the live environment without human intervention

practiceQuiz.hint: Which three specific tasks does Deployment Manager automate in a Pega DevOps workflow?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Branch merging, packaging and promotion are the named automation tasks.

optionExplanations.A: Branch merging, packaging and promotion are the named automation tasks.
optionExplanations.B: Automatic story generation is not the task stated here.
optionExplanations.C: The open approach also permits third-party tools.
optionExplanations.D: It does not promise all live testing happens without human involvement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO third-party tools are named as DevOps integration examples in the release-management v5 topic?

options.text: Jenkins
Microsoft Azure DevOps
Jira
GitHub Actions

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify named source examples; absence does not establish unsupported integration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Jenkins is a named DevOps example in this topic. Microsoft Azure DevOps is the other named example.

optionExplanations.A: Jenkins is a named DevOps example in this topic.
optionExplanations.B: Microsoft Azure DevOps is the other named example.
optionExplanations.C: Jira is a Workbench integration example, not named in this DevOps list.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Following the source’s continuous-delivery rollback strategy, a test fails after importing a package. What is the recommended action?

options.text: Roll back the latest import
Annotate the package as partially tested and continue
Skip the failing test and move to production
Create a feedback item and deploy anyway

practiceQuiz.hint: CD best practices include defining a rollback strategy in case tests fail post-deployment.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Roll back the latest import under the stated CD strategy.

optionExplanations.A: Roll back the latest import under the stated CD strategy.
optionExplanations.B: Partial-test annotation does not satisfy readiness.
optionExplanations.C: Skipping a failure disregards the stated strategy.
optionExplanations.D: A feedback item does not make the failed deployment ready.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer asks an SA about the relationship between Agile Studio and Agile Workbench when deciding how to track user stories and log bugs during an upcoming sprint in a Pega project. How does Agile Studio relate to Agile Workbench in Pega Platform?

options.text: Agile Studio is a separate Pega tool that expands Agile Workbench with release management, progress tracking, team capacity, and analytics
Agile Studio and Agile Workbench are the same tool with different names
Agile Studio is a simplified version of Agile Workbench for business analysts
Agile Studio replaces Agile Workbench in Pega Platform v8

practiceQuiz.hint: One expands the other with more robust capabilities.

optionExplanations.B: They are not two names for the same tool.
optionExplanations.C: Agile Studio adds capabilities rather than being a simpler Workbench.
optionExplanations.D: The source describes integration, not replacement in version 8.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is using Pega Agile Workbench to manage development work. Which TWO work item types can be created and tracked in Agile Workbench?

options.text: User Stories — describing a feature or capability from the end-user's perspective
Bugs — tracking defects identified during development, testing, or user acceptance
Sprint velocity reports — automatically generated productivity metrics from team commit activity
Server-provisioning metrics automatically generated by network monitoring

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify work item types rather than automatically generated metrics.
practiceQuiz.rationale: User Stories are one of the three named work item types. Bugs are the named defect-tracking work item type.

optionExplanations.A: User Stories are one of the three named work item types.
optionExplanations.B: Bugs are the named defect-tracking work item type.
optionExplanations.C: A generated velocity report is not one of those work item types.
optionExplanations.D: Generated network metrics are not one of those work item types.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega team is implementing CI/CD pipelines for a new Pega application. Which TWO statements correctly describe CI/CD pipeline behavior in Pega Platform?

options.text: A CI/CD pipeline automates the build, test, and deployment of Pega application changes across multiple environments
Pega Deployment Manager orchestrates the pipeline, coordinating automated tests and environment promotions
CI/CD pipelines in Pega always require a manual approval gate at every environment and cannot be fully automated
CI/CD pipelines in Pega replace all Ruleset versioning, eliminating the need for Branch Rulesets

practiceQuiz.hint: CI/CD automates build-test-deploy across environments; Deployment Manager is the orchestration tool.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The pipeline automates build, test and movement across environments. Deployment Manager provides orchestration for these workflows.

optionExplanations.A: The pipeline automates build, test and movement across environments.
optionExplanations.B: Deployment Manager provides orchestration for these workflows.
optionExplanations.C: The source permits automated delivery rather than mandatory gates everywhere.
optionExplanations.D: Versioned Rulesets and Branches remain relevant to development.

quickRecap.value: Stories, Bugs and Feedback. Change To do / Doing / Done by dragging or using the work item Status list.
Creating a new Case Type automatically creates a feature with the same name in Agile Workbench.
Guidance, Knowledge, Work, Checklists. Do not infer every tab is independently AI-powered.
CI: frequent check-ins, automated build, early issue detection. CD: staging → acceptance → preproduction → production with rollback.
If tests fail → STOP the release pipeline until fixed.
Admin Studio manages pipelines; integrated App Studio exposes Publishing. Automates merging, packaging and promotion.
Test environments (Docker or similar), regression tests, target versions, rollback strategy and readiness annotation; manual or automatic deployment.
